title: Summer jobs at Spanish Fort, West End and Milneburg camps
summary: Outdoor pavilion jobs at lakefront camps ran ten to six on Sundays, with food and about six dollars.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, they had dance halls down there, around Independent, around Independent Street. Then they had, uh, this place that I'll tell you about, this, uh, what they call it now? Oh, they have dancing in the breeze with the tarpoli, or the lawn dance, or something like that. They did that down there. Did they have trees, and dance under the trees? No, they were just, just, it was just an empty lot, and they covered it with the tarpoli and the dance. Did you ever play outdoor jokes with your band? I'm not talking about grassland. No, not, oh, yeah. I used to be talking about something, it reminded me. All the outdoor stuff I ever done was in, at Lake Punch and Train. Oh, I see. In these camps, they used to have camps out at Millenvoig, they had camps in West End, and they had camps in this other place out there, Bandit Fort. And during the summer months, it would be a rare thing to be on a Sunday. You'd go to work by ten o'clock in the morning and wait till six in the evening, in one of these clubs. You'd be in one place or the other, either Banish Fort, West End, or what you call it? That's the only outdoor work I ever done. And that wasn't exactly outdoors, because all these places have, uh, I might call it a shade. They all had a... Like a pavilion? Yeah, yeah. The oak,

Yeah, practically all of them had that. How was out at Spanish Fort Sunday looking at it? Yeah. How does it look? Well, there's nothing there except the ruins, you know. Yeah, yeah. But, but they must have had something out there more than that then. Yeah. And you know, people have built up new homes. Oh, you know, yeah. Yeah, but what was there?

Well, they had, well I'll tell you, the people had camps, what they call them. They had small houses, small buildings, what they used for Sundays and some of them used for vacation. That's on the edge of the bayou? On the lake itself? On the edge of the bayou and on the lake too. Oh, I see. Yeah. I guess what you said, you see the ruins out there, you must see some of these platforms that they had, built from the wharf to go out. Most of the camps was on the water. Oh, I see. And they had a platform from the, from the wharf to walk out to the camp.
At Spanish Fort all night, it looks like bricks from the actual fort itself. Yeah. Oh, yeah. That's Spanish Fort itself. Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Fort St. John. Yeah. When you played, you say you played all day from 10 to 6? Yeah, from 10 to 6, 10 in the morning to 16.

You think it was a hard job? Well, no, I'll tell you how that was. Wait, now that was a little decent. Because, you see, during the day, the people would stop to eat, some stopped to go swimming, and so on, so the band wouldn't have to do nothing. You know, while the people would stop to eat. Did they feed the band? Oh, yeah, yeah. They gave you all the drinks, food, about, excuse me, about six dollars a day, and all the food and drinks you could eat. Was that good pay? Well, I'll tell you. Well, I'll tell you. That was the best you could do. And everybody was paying about the same, so.
It was a pretty good job, you thought. Yeah, yeah, it was a pretty good job.

I mean, because it was always a very long job, you know. Yeah, yeah, from 10 to 6, you put it on, just eight hours. But I have to tell you, you'd get a time to rest, you know, while people went to swim, or stopped to eat.
You, the people would be dancing to your music at that, or you just entertained?

Well, they did dance, and people would be dancing under this pavilion, under this porch they had, like, all around the building, and dance on that floor all around the building. Were those private parties, or were they hired? Well, they were, they was, uh, practically all private parties, uh, uh, people wanting to do something, to have some fun on a Sunday, and they'd get together and do that. Would it be like, some kind of club? No admission, no admission, some, some clubs, yeah. But they weren't charging no admission. I mean, how many people would there be there, like? Oh, sometimes they had pretty good business. I wouldn't, couldn't estimate right now, but, well, pretty good business.
